rows.title: Texas Democrats in the U.S. House split on presidential nominee
rows.standfirst: Joe Biden has more endorsements from the Texas congressional delegation than either Texan in the race.

rows.title: “They’re just pushing us away”: Austin residents talk about homeless life amid Gov. Abbott’s criticism of city ordinances
rows.standfirst: Homeless residents in the state’s capital took varied paths to end up without shelter. And some who have found homes still return to homeless encampments to check in on friends.

rows.title: Empower Texans helped topple House Speaker Dennis Bonnen. Did it further the conservative movement?
rows.standfirst: The hardline conservative group can claim a victory for ousting Bonnen. But will that be good for its ideological interests?

rows.title: Texas voters evenly split on impeachment of Donald Trump, UT/TT Poll finds
rows.standfirst: Texas voters are divided on whether the president should be removed from office, but nearly half think impeachment investigations should proceed, according to the latest University of Texas/Texas Tribune Poll.

rows.title: Most Texas voters have heard nothing or little of the scandal that sunk House Speaker Dennis Bonnen, UT/TT Poll says
rows.standfirst: The recorded conversation that upended a first-term speaker of the Texas House was big news in state politics, but most registered voters barely noticed, according to the latest University of Texas/Texas Tribune Poll.

rows.title: Julián Castro raises $800,000 in 10-day span to stay in presidential race
rows.standfirst: With the money solidified, Castro’s campaign said it plans on making a push for the November and December Democratic primary debates — a lofty goal for a campaign that has been mired in low single digits in polls.

rows.title: Gutierrez to announce second run for Senate District 19
rows.standfirst: The seat is held by Pleasanton Republican Pete Flores, who won it in a special-election upset last year.

rows.title: Top HHS official to run FDA on temporary basis while Trump readies nomination of Texas cancer doctor
rows.standfirst: The president plans to nominate Stephen Hahn, the chief medical officer of Houston’s MD Anderson Cancer Center, as commissioner of the Food and Drug Administration.

rows.title: Beto O’Rourke drops out of presidential race
rows.standfirst: The former El Paso congressman announced the decision Friday.

rows.title: With financial challenges and frustrating polls, Beto O’Rourke’s campaign reaches an abrupt end
rows.standfirst: The former El Paso congressman’s withdrawal from the race for the White House came together relatively quickly with hours to spare before a major Democratic gathering in Iowa.

rows.title: Castro forges forward after 11th-hour fundraising drive, O’Rourke exit
rows.standfirst: The former U.S. housing secretary may have met a self-imposed deadline to raise $800,000 or end his campaign, but he still has his work cut out for him as the next Democratic debate approaches.

rows.title: Tenth Talks: Evan Smith on the next 10 years of media in Texas
rows.standfirst: In this episode of Tenth Talks, The Texas Tribune’s yearlong video series on the next 10 years of Texas, CEO Evan Smith says that “nonpartisan is a business model” and that the future of sustainability in local news depends on it.

rows.title: Tenth Talks: Watch four experts predict the future of Texas cities
rows.standfirst: In this edition of Tenth Talks, The Texas Tribune’s yearlong video series on the next 10 years of Texas, top leaders in housing, homelessness and transportation give Texas cities a decade’s worth of marching orders.

rows.title: T-Squared: The Texas Tribune is 10 years old today. Happy birthday to us — and to you.
rows.standfirst: On Nov. 3, 2009, when we flipped the switch on texastribune.org, we gave life to the idea that nonpartisan journalism in the public interest still matters. In the years since, you’ve put your faith in us to help you navigate the sometimes choppy waters of Texas.

rows.title: The one where Willie Nelson sings Happy Birthday to The Texas Tribune
rows.standfirst: What would Texas be without The Texas Tribune? Politicos, fellow journalists and yes, Willie Nelson, toast The Texas Tribune on our 10th anniversary.

rows.title: This school district has been at risk of state takeover for years. Some blame white flight.
rows.standfirst: In a 2003 lawsuit, Hearne Independent School District officials said the state’s failure to stop white students from transferring to a nearby district contributed to their academic struggles.

rows.title: Both sides brace for a more action-packed runoff in special election for Zerwas seat
rows.standfirst: The Tuesday special election for the suburban Houston seat is expected to advance to a runoff between the sole Democratic candidate and one of three viable Republican candidates out of six overall.

rows.title: U.S. Sen. John Cornyn’s rivals are unknown even to most Democratic voters, UT/TT Poll finds
rows.standfirst: The Democrats hoping to challenge Cornyn in the 2020 general election face a hurdle, according to the latest University of Texas/Texas Tribune Poll: Their own voters don’t know who they are.

rows.title: Democrats don’t have a candidate who would beat Trump in Texas today, poll finds
rows.standfirst: President Donald Trump would win head-to-head races with the top Democratic candidates right now, according to the latest University of Texas/Texas Tribune Poll.

rows.title: Analysis: Beto O’Rourke’s out, but he still casts a shadow on the 2020 Texas elections
rows.standfirst: Beto O’Rourke’s bid for the presidency failed. And he lost his 2018 bid for U.S. Senate. But he upended the status quo in Texas politics in ways that will play out in the 2020 elections.

rows.title: Happy birthday to us — and to you, our members!
rows.standfirst: Without the support of our members, The Texas Tribune wouldn’t be here today. Whether you’re a first-time member, a founding member or somewhere in between — THANK YOU for your support.

rows.title: Earthquakes in West Texas have dramatically increased, according to new University of Texas study
rows.standfirst: Every year West Texas experiences more and more small earthquakes. The study by the University of Texas at Austin documented more than 7,000 starting in 2009.

rows.title: Austin’s homeless residents say Abbott’s intervention is a short-term setback without a long-term solution
rows.standfirst: TxDOT began removing property and debris from under Austin’s highways as the number of places Austin ordinances let homeless people camp dwindles.

rows.title: Watch: A conversation on rural health care
rows.standfirst: We’re livestreaming our conversation in Canyon on rural health care, moderated by Texas Tribune Managing Editor Corrie MacLaggan.

rows.title: Election Day ballots feature 10 constitutional amendments, three vacant Texas House seats and one heated Houston mayoral race
rows.standfirst: Polls are open from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. today. One proposition could make it harder to create a state income tax while another could secure more funding for state parks. Here’s what you need to know.

rows.title: Voters are worried about leadership, border issues, health care and guns, UT/TT Poll finds
rows.standfirst: National leadership and border issues top the list of voter concerns about the country; at home, it’s the border and gun control, according to the latest University of Texas/Texas Tribune Poll.

rows.title: Texas shootings haven’t upended voters’ views on guns, UT/TT poll finds
rows.standfirst: A slim majority of Texans favor stricter gun laws, but voters have their limits, according to the latest University of Texas/Texas Tribune Poll

rows.title: Texas lawmakers ask Gov. Greg Abbott to stop execution of Rodney Reed, whose guilt is widely doubted
rows.standfirst: Rodney Reed’s guilt in the 1996 murder of Stacey Stites has been questioned for decades. A bipartisan group of lawmakers join national calls to stop his upcoming execution.

rows.title: Castro gets support of nine lawmakers who previously backed O’Rourke as he tries to shore up his campaign
rows.standfirst: The wave of endorsements comes four days after O’Rourke dropped out of the race — and as Castro searches for a path forward for his cash-strapped campaign.

rows.title: Federal judge hammers Texas officials over failures to improve foster care system
rows.standfirst: An exasperated U.S. District Judge Janis Graham Jack found the state in contempt of court for failing to comply with some of her earlier orders in the wide-ranging lawsuit filed on behalf of Texas foster children.

rows.title: In race to replace Zerwas in Texas House, Democrat Eliz Markowitz and Republican Gary Gates head to a runoff
rows.standfirst: Democrats are hoping to flip Texas House District 28 in the upcoming runoff. Meanwhile, in Dallas’ House District 100 race, five votes separate two candidates trying to make it to the second round.

rows.title: Texas voters approve state income tax ban, most other constitutional amendments
rows.standfirst: While voters supported most changes to the Texas Constitution, they opposed a measure that would allow elected municipal judges to work in more than one jurisdiction.

rows.title: Sylvester Turner to face Tony Buzbee in runoff for Houston mayor
rows.standfirst: Vote counting continued through the night. When results were released early Wednesday morning, the incumbent was short of the total he needed to avoid a runoff.

rows.title: On immigration issues, a wall between Texas partisans, UT/TT poll finds
rows.standfirst: Texas voters from the two major parties are split on a range of immigration issues, including immigration policy, deportations and bilingual education, according to the latest University of Texas/Texas Tribune Poll.

rows.title: Texans say climate change is happening, but it’s a highly partisan issue, UT/TT Poll finds
rows.standfirst: Most Texas voters say climate change is happening, but there are significant partisan differences, according to the latest University of Texas/Texas Tribune Poll.

rows.title: Texas executes Justen Hall for murder of woman in El Paso
rows.standfirst: Hall told a trial judge he needed “to be put down” in 2016. Lawyers questioned his mental health and asked an El Paso court to delay the execution until Hall’s competency can be evaluated.

rows.title: Texas 2019 constitutional amendment election results
rows.standfirst: Texas voters approved nine amendments to the state constitution, including a proposal making it harder to enact a personal income tax. One amendment was rejected.

rows.title: Bobby Moore’s death sentence is changed to life in prison after lengthy court fights over intellectual disability
rows.standfirst: Moore was sentenced to death in 1980 in the fatal shooting of an elderly store clerk during a Houston robbery.

rows.title: Half of registered Texas voters turned out in 2018. Just 12% turned out this year.
rows.standfirst: Turnout in odd-numbered years has always been historically low. While this year’s turnout is higher than in 2017, it’s still overwhelmingly low.

rows.title: Election results from Texas’ largest county were delayed for hours. What happened?
rows.standfirst: All Harris County election results had to be driven to downtown Houston with police escorts after state election officials objected to the county’s practice of uploading memory cards through an encrypted network.

rows.title: State to take over Houston ISD by replacing school board and superintendent
rows.standfirst: Texas Education Agency Commissioner Mike Morath informed Houston ISD of those plans in a letter Wednesday. He also sent letters saying the state would take over Shepherd and Snyder ISDs.

rows.title: “I wasn’t raised to be silent”: U.S. Rep. Filemon Vela is willing to tussle with colleagues from both parties
rows.standfirst: Earlier this year, U.S. Rep. Filemon Vela called a fellow Texan in Congress a “chicken-shit” in what became his latest clash with another politician.

rows.title: Texas cleared homeless camps Wednesday. On Thursday, residents were already back.
rows.standfirst: Gov. Greg Abbott announced a five-acre plot of land for homeless camping in Austin after he took action to clear people living under state overpasses.

rows.title: Federal judge delays execution of “Texas Seven” prisoner over claims of religious discrimination
rows.standfirst: For the second time, a court has stopped Murphy’s execution over concerns that the Texas prison system’s execution procedures discriminate against non-Christian inmates.

rows.title: TribCast: The UT/TT pollsters’ latest survey of Texas views on politics and policy
rows.standfirst: On this week’s special pollster edition of the TribCast, Ross talks to Josh Blank, Jim Henson and Daron Shaw from the University of Texas about the findings of the latest University of Texas/Texas Tribune Poll.

rows.title: TribCast: The 10th anniversary edition
rows.standfirst: On this week’s 10th anniversary TribCast, Emily talks to Evan, Ross, Todd and Reeve about the last 10 years of The Texas Tribune — and the last 10 years of the TribCast.

rows.title: Top Texas GOP donor resigns from company after admitting to prohibited contributions
rows.standfirst: James Dannenbaum, president and CEO of the high-powered Dannenbaum Engineering, was charged with a scheme to get employees to donate to three congressional candidates in 2017.

rows.title: U.S. Department of Education reviewing Texas State University’s compliance with a federal crime-reporting statute
rows.standfirst: The move comes after the university acknowledged it under-reported the number of rapes and other crimes on campus in recent years. Texas State’s president told students Thursday that the school is cooperating with the federal agency and has already made reforms.

rows.title: Secret recordings in Texas: A brief history of some Capitol controversies
rows.standfirst: Texas House Speaker Dennis Bonnen announced he would not seek reelection a week after the release of an infamous recording of a conversation between him and a political activist. It’s not the first time that secret recordings caused a stir in Texas politics.

rows.title: Someone has died on Texas roads every day for 19 years. Here’s a look at some reasons why — and ideas for turning the tide.
rows.standfirst: Ever since Nov. 8, 2000, someone has been killed in a Texas wreck each day. The state’s transportation department is spending an additional $600 million on safety — and trying to end all roadway deaths by 2050.

rows.title: Analysis: In Texas government, the buck stops … somewhere
rows.standfirst: Texas state government is run by top leaders who promised to model their operations on business. They didn’t say it would be an error-prone business.

rows.title: Exposing the 20 Medical Myths
rows.standfirst: Available now on Amazon, “Exposing the Twenty Medical Myths: Why Everything You Know About Health Care is Wrong and How to Make It Right,” provides an honest and unbiased view of the state of health care policy in America. Nationally-recognized health policy expert Dr. Tim Garson and former journalist Ryan Holeywell take a deep dive into the problems plaguing the health care system while also providing effective solutions to improve the health of the population.

rows.title: Serving Our Service Members Through Education
rows.standfirst: WGU Texas honors veterans every day through education programs tailored to veterans, transitioning and active-duty military members, and their families.

rows.title: T-Squared: New faces, new roles on the Trib’s editorial team
rows.standfirst: We’re thrilled to welcome some new faces to our newsroom — and to announce big new roles for two editors already on our team.

rows.title: State Rep. Poncho Nevárez won’t seek reelection in 2020
rows.standfirst: The Eagle Pass Democrat, who chairs the House Homeland Security and Public Safety Committee, announced the decision Friday, saying it’s “time to come home.”

rows.title: University of North Texas legal staffer resigns after using racist slur during a free speech panel
rows.standfirst: Assistant General Counsel Caitlin Sewell was speaking about speech protected by the First Amendment when she used the word. People in attendance vocally expressed offense.

rows.title: Texas Tech football coach defends his role in Utah State sexual assault scandal
rows.standfirst: A federal lawsuit filed this month alleges Coach Matt Wells failed to respond to sexual assault allegations.

rows.title: Two Texas Democrats have been campaigning in a statewide race that probably won’t be on the ballot
rows.standfirst: Amid confusion over the state’s mandatory retirement law, a state official confirmed to the Democratic Party months ago that the race for Texas Court of Criminal Appeals Place 6 would appear on the 2020 ballot. It probably won’t.

rows.title: After state takeover news, Houston ISD clams up, leaving parents and teachers scrambling for insight
rows.standfirst: The state’s announcement that it will seize control of its largest school system has been met with notable silence from Houston ISD administrators and local elected officials.

rows.title: Ted Cruz calls efforts to halt Rodney Reed’s execution “remarkable bipartisan coalition”
rows.standfirst: “If there is credible evidence there’s a real chance a defendant is innocent, that evidence should be weighed carefully,” Cruz tweeted Friday night.

rows.title: Sid Miller heard a Confederate group was excluded from a Veteran’s Day parade. His Facebook response? “Get a rope.”
rows.standfirst: Miller, Texas’ Agriculture Commissioner, has a history of making inflammatory, offensive and false posts on social media.

rows.title: Kay Granger is the most senior Republican woman in the U.S. House. But her reelection could turn into an intra-GOP battle.
rows.standfirst: Granger, who is seeking a 13th term representing her Fort Worth district, already has at least one well-funded Republican primary challenger in Chris Putnam. Some Republicans are bracing for the March primary to turn into a nationalized battle.

rows.title: Analysis: In Texas politics, a little ignorance can lead to bliss
rows.standfirst: Not paying attention to every political move isn’t a sign of civic disengagement. It might just be a sign of a balanced life.

rows.title: Two of U.S. Energy Secretary Rick Perry’s political supporters won “potentially lucrative” Ukraine energy deal, report says
rows.standfirst: The Associated Press reports that the oil and gas exploration contract was awarded after Perry recommended one of his backers as an energy adviser to Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelensky.

rows.title: Texas had 7 mass shootings over 10 years. Meanwhile, gun control has loosened statewide.
rows.standfirst: Texas has a history of deadly mass shootings. Many have sparked public debate about what legislation should be passed to prevent another one.

rows.title: Joe Biden ramps up Texas campaign, naming state director
rows.standfirst: The Democratic presidential candidate is also getting support from another Texas state senator, Burleson’s Beverly Powell.

rows.title: Trump administration tells Supreme Court it owns termination of DACA program
rows.standfirst: The U.S. Supreme Court heard opening oral arguments Tuesday on the legality of the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals program.

rows.title: A Trump administration strategy led to the child migrant backup crisis at the border
rows.standfirst: Interviews, emails and memos detailing the strategy show that officials knew that without enough beds in government shelters, children would languish in Border Patrol stations not equipped to care for them.

rows.title: In Texas case, Supreme Court wrestles with the legal boundaries of cross-border shootings
rows.standfirst: A U.S. Border Patrol Agent in El Paso fired across the border and killed a Mexican teen in 2010. The justices will decide whether the teen’s family can sue the U.S. government.

rows.title: Julián Castro missed the cutoff for the November debate. Now what?
rows.standfirst: His campaign is suggesting that it no longer sees having a national platform as a must. Instead, it’s staking its hopes on a strong finish in Iowa, Nevada and Castro’s home state of Texas.

rows.title: As Trump impeachment hearings go public, previous transcripts shed light on roles Texas lawmakers may play
rows.standfirst: In closed-door testimony, Republican Texans in Congress pushed back against witnesses and criticized fellow lawmakers while Democrats remained largely quiet. Transcripts from those hearings may portend what happens during the inquiry’s public phase.

rows.title: Analysis: For Texas candidates, 2020 officially started last weekend
rows.standfirst: The starting gun wasn’t loud, but the 2020 elections in Texas began — officially — last Saturday, when candidates could start filing for office. That’s the beginning of a sprint from now to the March primaries.

rows.title: Retiring U.S. Rep. Will Hurd endorses candidate to succeed him
rows.standfirst: The Helotes Republican gave his support Wednesday to former Navy officer Tony Gonzales.

rows.title: U.S. Rep. Ratcliffe emerges as strong defender of Trump during public hearing on impeachment
rows.standfirst: See what the Texans in Congress are asking the witnesses in today’s public impeachment inquiry hearing.

rows.title: Introducing Teach Me How to Texas, a newsletter for Texas voters
rows.standfirst: Subscribers will learn interesting facts about Texas’ past and culture, how to spot a good poll from a bad one, how to decode their November ballots and more.

rows.title: Appeals court overturns mandate for Texas to implement online voter registration for drivers
rows.standfirst: A lower court previously ruled that Texas was violating federal law by failing to register residents to vote when they updated their driver’s licenses online and ordered the state to implement its first system of online voter registration.

rows.title: TribCast: Sid Miller’s Facebook rhetoric, Rodney Reed finds bipartisan allies
rows.standfirst: On this week’s TribCast, Emily talks to Ross, Emma and Jolie about Ag Commissioner Sid Miller’s latest Facebook rhetoric, the escalating pressure on the governor in the Rodney Reed death penalty case and a court of criminal appeals race that has everything going for it but an actual election.

rows.title: Texas education board likely to approve African American studies course in 2020
rows.standfirst: “We will be passing this,” said Pat Hardy, a Republican on the Texas State Board of Education.

rows.title: President Donald Trump to tour Apple facilities in Texas on Wednesday
rows.standfirst: Trump will tour a new Apple manufacturing plant in Austin on Wednesday with Apple CEO Tim Cook.

rows.title: Toxic algae blooms that kill dogs are becoming more common. And climate change is making it worse, scientists say.
rows.standfirst: A toxic algae bloom in Austin that killed five dogs caught officials by surprise, but despite how dangerous the blooms are, there’s almost no way for cities to combat them.

rows.title: Optimistic Democrats are lining up to run for Texas’ high courts in 2020
rows.standfirst: The depth of the bench for non-marquee statewide races, like the state’s two high courts and the Railroad Commission, is a measure of how high Democratic hopes have soared ahead of the 2020 election.

rows.title: As Walmart reopens, El Pasoans are still grappling with mass shooting’s aftermath
rows.standfirst: The store where a gunman killed nearly two dozen people and shot dozens more in August opened its doors Thursday, setting off a wave of mixed emotions in a community still grieving.

rows.title: Arrest warrant issued for state Rep. Poncho Nevárez after he was caught on tape dropping envelope with cocaine
rows.standfirst: The document says that the envelope had Nevárez’s official House seal and held “four small clear baggies” containing a substance found to include cocaine.

rows.title: UT System increases tuition 2.6% for all campuses for 2020 and 2021
rows.standfirst: Chancellor J.B. Milliken said 2.6% is the rate of inflation in the higher education sector. UT institutions have increased tuition between 0.1% and 8.5% in recent years.

rows.title: Apprehensions of undocumented immigrants on the Southwest border continue to fall
rows.standfirst: The figure is the lowest since July 2018 and marks the fifth consecutive month that the number has dropped.

rows.title: U.S. Rep. Will Hurd rolls out group to build more diverse GOP
rows.standfirst: The Future Leaders Fund, a super PAC, plans to spend millions of dollars in the 2020 primaries.

rows.title: Texas education officials face local resistance to Houston ISD board takeover
rows.standfirst: Houston ISD parents and residents made it clear Thursday night that they don’t want the state to replace their elected school board.

rows.title: Analysis: Two Texas House scandals, unrelated but linked
rows.standfirst: Topically, a state legislator’s cocaine possession case and the intemperate conversation that undid the speaker of the Texas House aren’t related. But both are fodder for anyone who wants to shake up state government.

rows.title: Pressure is mounting to stop Rodney Reed’s execution. Where does his case stand?
rows.standfirst: Dozens of lawmakers — both Republicans and Democrats — have asked Gov. Greg Abbott and the parole board to stop Reed’s execution. There are also multiple appeals in the courts.

rows.title: Elizabeth Warren expands Texas campaign, naming senior staff
rows.standfirst: The Democratic presidential candidate now has easily the biggest organization devoted to the state of any primary campaign.

rows.title: State Rep. Poncho Nevárez turns himself in to authorities after dropping envelope with cocaine
rows.standfirst: The Eagle Pass Democrat was caught on video surveillance dropping an envelope of cocaine on the ground at the Austin airport.

rows.title: Texas court stops Rodney Reed’s execution to further review claims of innocence
rows.standfirst: The ruling came hours after the Texas parole board recommended that Gov. Greg Abbott delay Reed’s death for 120 days.

rows.title: The inauguration of Greg Abbott and Dan Patrick cost millions. But much of it went to fundraising and staff.
rows.standfirst: Spending on each of the last two inaugurations eclipsed that of any other in Texas for at least 40 years, even when adjusted for inflation. A spokesman for the governor has said no state dollars were spent on the festivities.

rows.title: Analysis: Beware of Texas politicians bearing home-brewed arithmetic
rows.standfirst: When government officials want to spin a story about state finance, it helps to have control of the numbers — and to do the math properly.

rows.title: Here’s a list of Texas organizations that are helping the homeless
rows.standfirst: Texas officials have waged a social media war over how best to approach homelessness. Experts say one way Texans can help is to reach out to local organizations and see what they need.

rows.title: Texas athletes could make money from pending NCAA rule changes. How much? It’s not yet clear.
rows.standfirst: The NCAA’s proposed rule changes could let prominent athletes generate major endorsement money. But for most athletes, there won’t likely be much of a windfall.

rows.title: Former Texas House Speaker Joe Straus calls on Supreme Court to protect workplace rights for LGBTQ Americans
rows.standfirst: Straus’ op-ed comes a month after the U.S. Supreme Court heard oral arguments for three employment discrimination cases in which a person was fired for being gay or transgender.

rows.title: T-Squared: Emily Ramshaw and Amanda Zamora launching a national news organization for women
rows.standfirst: They’ll exit their leadership roles at The Texas Tribune at the end of the year. We couldn’t be more grateful for all they’ve done for us — or prouder of what they’re about to do.

rows.title: With Bonnen sidelined, House Republicans spearhead new PAC to protect majority
rows.standfirst: The group, Leading Texas Forward PAC, hopes to raise $5 million this cycle, according to one of the lawmakers involved. Karl Rove is the group’s treasurer.

rows.title: Federal judge issues partial block of Trump administration’s third-country asylum rule
rows.standfirst: A U.S. district judge ruled the administration’s third-country rule doesn’t apply to people who sought asylum before July 16.

rows.title: Donald Trump touted Apple manufacturing jobs in Austin on Wednesday. Here’s what you need to know.
rows.standfirst: Trump toured a newly expanded Apple manufacturing plant in Austin and incorrectly tweeted afterward that he’d opened the plant. The plant has been open since before Trump’s term began.

rows.title: Rodney Reed’s execution was set for Wednesday. A Texas court stopped it last week.
rows.standfirst: The Texas Tribune takes a look at Reed’s case as it is sent back to the local court, which will review claims that he is innocent of the murder that put him on death row.

rows.title: Analysis: The Texas House is looking for new leadership — and maybe a change in direction
rows.standfirst: The Texas House is right where it was two years ago, entering an uncertain election cycle with a lame-duck leader. Does that signal a new path?

rows.title: U.S. ambassador on Rick Perry, Rudy Giuliani and Ukraine: “We did not want to work with Mr. Giuliani”
rows.standfirst: Gordon Sondland testified Wednesday that Giuliani, President Donald Trump’s personal attorney, pushed a quid pro quo between the American and Ukrainian leadership. The ambassador confirmed he worked closely with Perry, the outgoing energy secretary, on Ukrainian policy.

rows.title: Texas isn’t providing major support for the 2020 Census. Local officials and nonprofits say they will instead.
rows.standfirst: Several nonprofits, local governments and philanthropy organizations have formed Texas Counts, a coalition aimed at ensuring an accurate census count in 2020, which could affect representation in Congress and billions in federal funding.

rows.title: Tribcast: A Texas House cocaine scandal and a lack of receipts for the latest inauguration celebration
rows.standfirst: In this edition of the TribCast, Alex talks to Evan, Cassi and Shannon about the latest scandal to rock the Texas House, the receipts — or lack thereof — for Gov. Greg Abbott and Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick’s inauguration ceremony, and Julián Castro missing the fifth Democratic primary debate.

rows.title: Michael Bloomberg files paperwork to get on the Texas primary ballot
rows.standfirst: Bloomberg is the fourth person to file for the Democratic presidential primary in Texas.

rows.title: South Texas is known for its moderates. A primary challenge to U.S. Rep. Henry Cuellar could test that.
rows.standfirst: Jessica Cisneros, a 26-year-old immigration attorney, is running to unseat Cuellar, one of the most conservative Democrats in Congress.

rows.title: As government prepares to seize more land for a border wall, some Texas landowners prepare to fight
rows.standfirst: In Laredo, border landowners are receiving letters from the federal government, requesting permission to enter their land for surveying. “Hell no, we’re not signing anything,” one recipient said.

rows.title: In key vote, federal regulators OK controversial South Texas gas export facilities
rows.standfirst: A coalition of residents and indigenous and environmental groups has rallied against a trio of proposed terminals to export liquefied natural gas from the Port of Brownsville. Thursday’s vote puts the terminals closer to final approval.

rows.title: Trump EPA eases safety requirements enacted after West explosion
rows.standfirst: Attorney General Ken Paxton applauded the new rules, saying they would make Texans safer. The Obama-era regulation was meant to improve chemical safety practices and prevent tragedies like the deadly 2013 fertilizer plant explosion in the tiny Central Texas town of West.

rows.title: U.S. Rep. Will Hurd sticks with Republicans during last public impeachment hearing of the week
rows.standfirst: Some Democrats hoped U.S. Rep. Will Hurd, a moderate Republican, would defect from his colleagues in the House Intelligence Committee. He came close but made clear he’s not ready to impeach.

rows.title: Gov. Greg Abbott orders state agencies to reduce licensing regulations, cut fees
rows.standfirst: Abbott has set a Dec. 1 deadline for agencies to tell his office how they plan to limit regulations, reduce fees and, “where appropriate,” remove licensing barriers for people with criminal records.

rows.title: Analysis: Whatever color Texas is, everybody’s running like it’s purple
rows.standfirst: Texas has been solidly Republican for a long time, but candidates and political people on both sides are sure acting like the state is competitive.

rows.title: San Antonio paid sick leave requirement blocked by state judge
rows.standfirst: A judge blocked an ordinance that would provide paid sick leave for employees who work in the city of San Antonio starting Dec. 1.

rows.title: Trump administration to shuttle migrants from Tucson to El Paso under “Remain in Mexico” policy
rows.standfirst: The policy hasn’t started in Arizona, so the government plans to bus migrants to El Paso, then send many of them to Ciudad Juárez while their asylum claims are pending, administration sources say.

rows.title: Texas AG Ken Paxton joins effort to stop Fort Worth hospital from removing 9-month-old girl from life support
rows.standfirst: The case centers around the Texas Advance Directives Act, a controversial law that allows doctors to end treatment for patients when further care is deemed futile.

rows.title: Feds order Texas Education Agency to pay fired special education director more than $200,000
rows.standfirst: The U.S. Department of Education found that Laurie Kash’s disclosures about how the TEA awarded a contract were “contributing factors” in her termination.

rows.title: Analysis: Why Texas Republicans are launching trial balloons on gun laws
rows.standfirst: Two University of Texas/Texas Tribune pollsters say top state officials edging into slightly tighter gun control laws are taking their cues from the changing electoral climate — not from changing attitudes among voters.

rows.title: Prison health care costs are higher than ever in Texas. Many point to an aging prison population.
rows.standfirst: Although there are fewer people in prison than there were a decade ago, costs have surged along with the share of inmates who are older — and sicker.

rows.title: Analysis: The middle is intriguing but uncrowded in Texas politics
rows.standfirst: In a state that has been closely tied to conservative politics for decades, some Texas politicians are edging into a political desert: the middle.

rows.title: Michael Bloomberg spends $3 million on Texas TV ads as he rolls out presidential bid
rows.standfirst: The 60-second spots will air on broadcast television in the Austin, Dallas-Fort Worth, El Paso, Harlingen-Weslaco, Houston and San Antonio markets.

rows.title: Translators help Korean American voters in Harris County find their electoral voice
rows.standfirst: After years of relying on volunteer translators, Korean Americans voting in Houston last month received help from newly hired bilingual poll workers.

rows.title: Jared Kushner’s new assignment: Overseeing the construction of Trump’s border wall
rows.standfirst: President Donald Trump has set an aggressive goal: building more than 400 miles of new barrier by the end of 2020. That will require quickly seizing lots of private land in Texas.

rows.title: UT-Austin investigating former procurement official after review finds irregularities
rows.standfirst: The former assistant vice president is the second University of Texas official to face scrutiny in recent months for allegedly running afoul of the university’s financial processes. He now holds a similar position with Austin ISD.

rows.title: As experienced Texas congressmen retire, will the state’s sway in Congress decline?
rows.standfirst: Last year, the Texas congressional delegation had six chairmanships in the U.S. House. Now it only has one.

rows.title: Analysis: Almost nothing in Texas government has unanimous consent
rows.standfirst: State officials say local governments shouldn’t use taxpayer funds for things some taxpayers don’t support. That describes just about everything government does.

rows.title: T-Squared: Regina Mack is returning to The Texas Tribune
rows.standfirst: Before she spent a year as Texas Monthly’s social media editor, Mack was an engagement fellow at The Texas Tribune. We couldn’t be more excited she’s coming back.

rows.title: Port Neches plant rocked by multiple explosions has history of environmental missteps
rows.standfirst: The Southeast Texas chemical manufacturing plant, owned by Houston-based Texas Petroleum Chemical Group, has been fined multiple times by state and federal regulators for air pollution violations.
